Every evaluation is a billed model call on the org, so do not author one where a "conditional" filter would answer the same question. Note this node IS available on APPOINTMENT graphs even though "conditional" is not. CONTACT actions: "text_action" (SMS to the contact; allowed only in workflowType TEXT; config {mode:"single", textBody or templateId} | {mode:"multiple", textBodies:[...]} (rotates one per send) | {mode:"generative", systemPrompt}); "email_action" (only in workflowType EMAIL; config {emailBody, emailSubject?} | {templateId} | {generate:true, systemPrompt}); "notification_action" (text a TEAMMATE, not the contact; config {recipientType:"POINT_PERSON"} | {recipientType:"SPECIFIC_USER", recipientUserId} | {recipientType:"PHONE_NUMBER", recipientPhoneNumber}, always with textBody); "tags_action" (apply tags; config {tagIds:[...]}); "add_user_group_action" (add the contact to team(s), optionally auto-assigning an agent from a team; config {userGroupIds:[...], agentAssignment?: {kind:"NONE"} | {kind:"TEAM_ROUND_ROBIN", userGroupId} | {kind:"SPECIFIC_USER", userId}}); "contributors_action" (attach users to the contact; config {contributors:[{userId, status:"POINT_PERSON"|"PARTICIPANT"}], roundRobin?:{userIds:[...], role} — its presence switches to round-robin: one user per run, rotating. TWO REQUIRED BOOLEANS, both rejected if omitted rather than defaulted: sendNotificationToContributor notifies the user who was added/assigned, and replaceExistingAgent decides whether an Agent this step picks may DISPLACE the contact's current Agent — with it false, a contact that already has an Agent keeps it and the pick is added as a Participant instead. They are required because a silent default is what an omission used to get, and it was the WRONG one: the editor seeds both false on a new node while an omitted field meant the old notify-and-replace behaviour, so the same node authored two ways behaved differently. Send both; false, false is what the builder gives a new node); "set_custom_field_action" (config {customFieldId, customFieldName, customFieldType:"TEXT"|"NUMBER"|"DOLLAR"|"DATE"|"DROPDOWN"|"LINK"} plus the matching value field textValue | numberValue | dateIso | dropdownOptionId); "task_action" (create a task; config {name, taskType, dueOffset:{amount, unit:"DAYS"|"WEEKS"|"MONTHS"}, preferredTimeOfDay:{hour, minute, timezone}, assigneeUserIds:[...], usePointPersonAssignee?, description?, createGoogleCalendarEvent?}); "appointment_action" (like task_action with {startOffset, preferredStartTimeOfDay, durationMinutes, attendeeUserIds}); "deal_action" (create a deal; config {title, pipelineId, stageId, propertyConfig:"none"|"add_all_verified_properties"|"add_all_properties"|"add_first_verified_property", assigneeUserIds?, usePointPersonAssignee?, description?}); "ai_employee_action" (put an AI employee on the contact; config {agentId, runNow:boolean, schedule?:{cronExpression, timezone, maxRuns}}); "send_webhook_action" (config {urls:[...]}); "send_slack_action" (config {slackChannelId, slackChannelName, message:{text, blocks?}}); "trigger_contact_workflow_action" (start other contact workflows on this contact; config {workflowGroupIds:[...]}). DEAL actions: "assign_to_user_action" ({userIds:[...]}), "notification_action" ({recipientType:"DEAL_USERS"} | {recipientType:"SPECIFIC_USERS", userIds}, always with textBody), "create_deal_action" (same config as CONTACT deal_action), "send_slack_action", "trigger_contact_workflow_action". PROPERTY actions: "create_contact_action" ({contactListIds?, triggerContactWorkflowGroupIds?, contributorUserIds?, assignAgent?:{mode:"single_user", userId} | {mode:"round_robin", userIds}, deal?, and ONE REQUIRED BOOLEAN, rejected if omitted rather than defaulted: replaceExistingAgent, which decides whether an Agent this step picks may DISPLACE the contact's current one — this is a find-or-create, so it lands on contacts that already have an owner, and displacing DELETES the previous owner's mapping rather than demoting them to Participant. It is required because an omission used to mean `true`, and the editor seeds `false` on a new node, so the same node authored two ways behaved differently. Send `false` unless you mean to displace), "add_to_list_action" ({listIds:[...]}), "send_slack_action", "send_webhook_action". APPOINTMENT actions: "text_action" (single mode only), "trigger_contact_workflow_action", "send_slack_action". EVENT actions (config values are accessor paths into the webhook payload): "find_create_contact_action" ({mode:"field_mapping", nameAccessor, phoneAccessors?, emailAccessors?, propertyAddressAccessors?, mailingAddressAccessors?, noteAccessors?} | {mode:"transformer", hint?}), "event_find_property_action" (flat config; resolutionMode:"full_address"|"address_components"|"parcel_id"|"transformer", actionType:"add_to_list"|"skiptrace"|"skiptrace_create_contact", plus the accessor/id fields each mode needs), "event_send_slack_action" ({slackChannelId?, slackChannelName?, message} — plain text with {{accessor}} placeholders). A node type you see in a stored graph but not in this list is RETIRED (parse-compat only): never author one and never copy one into a new graph. Triggers are managed through the `triggers` array: each entry is upserted by its id (mint a fresh UUID to add one) and entries omitted from the array are detached; only `config` syncs (`name` is cosmetic). Trigger config shapes: {type: "manual"}, {type: "created"}, {type: "mutation", filter: <FilterGroup>}, {type: "match", filter: <FilterGroup>}; CONTACT-only: {type: "inbound_text", twilioPhoneNumberIds: [...]}, {type: "inbound_email", connectedAccountIds?: [...]}; EVENT workflows have exactly one trigger shape, {type: "event_received"} — the workflow's minted webhook URL is the trigger. Minimal valid drip example (node/edge shape): nodes: [{id:"n1",type:"trigger",config:{}}, {id:"n2",type:"text_action",config:{mode:"single",textBody:"Hi {{firstName}}"}}, {id:"n3",type:"wait",config:{mode:"fixed",seconds:172800,interruptEnabled:false,interruptFilter:{id:"f1",operator:"AND",conditions:[],groups:[]}}}, {id:"n4",type:"end",config:{}}], edges: [{id:"e1",config:{},parentNodeId:"n1",childNodeId:"n2"}, {id:"e2",config:{},parentNodeId:"n2",childNodeId:"n3"}, {id:"e3",config:{},parentNodeId:"n3",childNodeId:"n4"}]. PROMOTE GOTCHA: a template-less TEXT/EMAIL draft starts with communicationConfig.sender {type: "UNSET"}, and promoteWorkflowDraft rejects SenderNotChosen — set a real sender in the automation config (e.g. {type: "POINT_PERSON"}) before promoting; getWorkflow.draftValidation names this and any other blocking issues. GRAPH CONFIG — `graph.config`, the settings an operator asks for by name. It sits beside `nodes`/`edges`/`triggers` and is NOT per-node. Shared keys (every domain): `triggerOperator` "AND"|"OR" (whether a graph with several triggers needs all of them or any one); `activation.triggerEligibleRecordsNow` (on activation, enroll records that ALREADY match, not just future ones); and `triggerWindow`, which limits when ENROLLMENT may happen; `exclusiveEnrollment` true means a record entering THIS workflow is unenrolled from every OTHER workflow it is still running under — those runs are STOPPED at the moment this one is created (other WORKFLOW, so a prior version of this same workflow is left alone), which is how "only one campaign at a time per lead" is expressed. It is inert on EVENT graphs, whose runs anchor on a webhook payload rather than a record. CONTACT graphs add `exitConditions.exitConditionTypes` — any of "any_inbound_communication", "inbound_text", "inbound_email", "contact_archived" — which is how "stop the drip as soon as they reply" is expressed; there is no per-node way to say it. APPOINTMENT graphs accept the `exitConditions` key but it carries nothing (typed `undefined`), so exit conditions are effectively CONTACT-only. `communicationConfig` is NOT contact-only: CONTACT and APPOINTMENT graphs both take it, and it is where an appointment reminder's quiet hours and sender live too. SEND WINDOW — `sendWindow` (on communicationConfig) and `triggerWindow` (top level) are the same shape: {timezone, daysOfWeek?:["MON".."SUN"], startTime?:{hour,minute}, endTime?:{hour,minute}}. `hour` AND `minute` are BOTH REQUIRED on each time — {hour:9} alone is rejected by the graph parser. These are clock times, not offsets, so "weekdays 9-6 Central" is daysOfWeek MON..FRI with startTime {hour:9,minute:0} and endTime {hour:18,minute:0}. A channel that configures NOTHING is not unrestricted: it falls back to 08:00-21:00 Eastern, the TCPA envelope. Say that rather than implying a missing window means any hour. SENDER — `communicationConfig` selects who a message comes FROM, and a mode name alone is not a valid sender: most modes carry required fields. TEXT: {type:"UNSET"} | {type:"POINT_PERSON"} | {type:"MEETING_OWNER"} (appointment graphs) | {type:"PHONE", fromPhoneNumberId} | {type:"RANDOM_PHONE", fromPhoneNumberIds:[...]} | {type:"LOCAL_PRESENCE", scope, fallback} — LOCAL_PRESENCE picks a team number whose area code matches the recipient, and BOTH scope and fallback are required: scope is {kind:"ALL_TEAM"} | {kind:"SPECIFIC", fromPhoneNumberIds} | {kind:"EXCLUDE", excludedPhoneNumberIds} | {kind:"MARKETING_CAMPAIGN", ...}, and a MARKETING_CAMPAIGN scope accepts ONLY the {type:"SCOPE_POOL"} fallback. EMAIL: {type:"UNSET"} | {type:"POINT_PERSON"} | {type:"IDENTITY", fromEmail, fromClientId} | {type:"RANDOM_IDENTITY", identities:[...]}. UNSET is the creation default and activation is GATED on replacing it, so a graph left on UNSET will not run. SYSTEM CATEGORY — the separate `systemCategory` variable, not part of the graph. CONTACT, DEAL, EVENT and APPOINTMENT all allow CUSTOM workflows, so `null` is correct there — do NOT attach a category to make an appointment reminder. PROPERTY is the one domain that allows no custom workflow at all: it MUST carry "PROPERTY_SIGNAL_SKIP_TRACE" (or "PROPERTY_SIGNAL_SKIP_TRACE_UNLIMITED", the entitlement-gated unthrottled variant), and creating one without a category is rejected with "Custom workflows are not available for property — pick a template." A non-null `systemCategory` ALSO requires a `templateId` on the same create — "A system-category workflow needs a template id" — so a category alone still fails. Both rejections read as "property workflows are not supported" if you do not know the pair is required. One category exists that NO domain offers at create time: "APPOINTMENT_REMINDER" is a stored value you may READ on an existing workflow, but nothing lists it as creatable, so never pass it on a create — the appointment domain takes custom workflows instead.
